findings.failure_path: MPR_SKILL#069 and MPR_PDA#068 claim one operative carrier at MPR_ECPM:37. The supplied MPR_PDC:91 also requires a complete denominator or gold set, directs researchers to mark recall unknown without one, and bars reporting a recall lower bound, population size, or proportions. Both rules govern organization research, so counting the selected destination alone produces a false single-carrier result.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep one operative recall-denominator rule and replace the overlapping guidance with a pointer. Regenerate the affected rows and show that the verifier rejects a duplicate placed elsewhere in the package.

findings.failure_path: MPR_SKILL#090 credits four checker failure shapes to MPR_ECPM:62. That line contains only the lost-shell-environment case. The other three are on lines 63 through 65. The supplied MPR_PDC excerpt confirms the text at line 78 but begins below its cited heading.
findings.smallest_fix: Map the four cases to their operative lines or cite the full block. Attach candidate-numbered destination text with the governing headings for the remaining locators.

findings.failure_path: The row claims output-directory containment for cache acceptance, staging, and publication. The packet contains no candidate recipe or fixtures for the prior deeper-symlink, traversal, and newline cases. M24 reports rejection and no file creation for one outside path. That result leaves open whether existing-file acceptance and publication both use the verified destination.
findings.smallest_fix: Attach the numbered recipe from destination validation through cache acceptance, staging, and publication, with the exact-candidate assertions for both existing-file and missing-file cases and a valid nested destination.

findings.failure_path: M28 reports that one fixture detects an empty expected inventory. The full manifest, matching predicates, and normal invocation are absent. The packet therefore cannot establish that the normal invocation rejects an omitted inventory, that co-deleting a recipe and its registration stays red, or that two registrations cannot claim the same fence.
findings.smallest_fix: Attach the complete candidate inventory and matcher, the normal invocation, and the exact-candidate assertions for omitted inventory, co-deletion, and overlapping matches.

findings.failure_path: The recorded namespace predicate shows a brace followed by a quote. An ordinary ElementTree expanded tag begins with a brace followed by the namespace URI. The packet gives no parser or write-path excerpt to resolve the discrepancy and no assertions showing that rejected XML preserves last-run.json or that an invalid later batch item prevents an earlier valid item from being written.
findings.smallest_fix: Correct the predicate description against the candidate and attach the parser and batch preflight excerpts with the final-state assertions for baseline preservation and zero writes.

concern_results.conclusion: All 225 MPR rows contain a positive line number and an untruncated heading. The first row now reaches operative text, and both PDC survivor passages are supplied. Destination text is missing for 97 rows, and one visible locator covers only the first of four claimed cases.

The packet gives the intended output-directory protections and one outside-write mutation result. The recipe and fixtures needed to verify that cache acceptance, staging, and publication all respect the same boundary are missing.

The packet describes deeper symlink, traversal, newline, and malformed-input cases. It omits the implementation and assertions needed to verify cache reuse, retry and cleanup, and preservation of existing state after a rejected operation.

The T4 baseline now distinguishes live and dangling leaf symlinks, consistent with the register. The suite totals and mutation summaries leave the full MANIFEST matching predicates and several named boundary assertions unverified.

The three landing files introduce no executable switch, permission, rollout restriction, or compatibility layer. The reported tests leave ordinary nested output and existing-cache behavior under the referenced guard unverified.

The landing files change documentation and evidence. Release acceptance is still recorded as pending, and the packet does not establish that the referenced report and batch-write paths preserve existing state on failure.

The register and validation ledger agree on the T4 suite total, lint result, and cited mutations. The release ledger lacks the item-9 verdict locator and diagnostics that an operator needs to identify a blocked input, label, or step.
Row 924 escapes the literal pipes and preserves the five-column table. The package-wide single-carrier claim is contradicted by operative recall-denominator guidance in both supplied references.

The packet does not establish enforcement of the shared release gate or the referenced write-finality protections. Missing evidence includes the item-9 blocking verdict, the guarded publication path, and the report and batch-write failure assertions.

The quoted AGENTS.md is unchanged, and the packet demonstrates no conflicting or obsolete contract rule. The profile identifies some checks at the exact candidate, while the broader local-lane results appear only as ledger assertions.
